description: Building the model geometry in COMSOL Multiphysics 6.3: 3D and 2D primitives, work planes and the work-plane operations (Extrude, Revolve, Sweep), Boolean and partition operations, transforms, fillets, the Form Union/Assembly finalization step, and CAD/mesh import. Every node is a feature in an ordered geometry sequence created with model.component(<ctag>).geom(<gtag>).create(<ftag>, <type>) and built with geom.run(); the feature type strings below are the exact second argument of create().

tools.name: Block
tools.description: Creates a right-angled solid or surface box in 3D, the most common building brick for enclosures, substrates, air domains and subtraction tools. You give the three edge lengths in size and a corner or centre position in pos, and can tilt the block by giving a local z-axis direction and a rotation about it. The layer properties slice the block into parallel layers on any chosen face, which is the quickest way to build a stacked structure as a single object.
tools.usage: Component 1 > Geometry 1 > right-click > Block   (Geometry toolbar > Block)

parameters.name: size
parameters.description: double[] {lx, ly, lz} - the three edge lengths. Default {1,1,1}.

parameters.name: pos
parameters.description: double[] position of the block. Default {0,0,0}.

parameters.name: base
parameters.description: corner (default) - pos is a corner; center - pos is the centre of the block.

parameters.name: axis / axistype
parameters.description: Direction of the local z-axis; axistype is x, y, z (default z), cartesian (3-vector) or spherical (2 angles).

parameters.name: rot
parameters.description: Rotation angle about axis, in the geometry's angular unit. Default 0.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: solid (default) or surface.

parameters.name: layer, layertop, layerbottom, layerleft, layerright, layerfront, layerback
parameters.description: Thicknesses of layers and which faces they are applied from; layerbottom is on by default.

parameters.name: selresult / selresultshow / contributeto
parameters.description: Create selections of the resulting objects, choose which entity levels are exposed outside the sequence, and contribute to a cumulative selection.

tools.notes: size, pos and axis accept a double[], a space- or comma-separated string ("1 2.1 0.5") or a String[] of parameter expressions, which is how a parameterized geometry is normally written. Hexahedron builds a general six-faced solid from eight corner points, Pyramid a rectangular pyramid or frustum, and Tetrahedron a tetrahedron - all on the More Primitives menu. The legacy type strings block2 (solid) and block3 (surface) still work.

tools.name: Cylinder
tools.description: Creates a right circular solid or surface cylinder in 3D from a radius, a height, a base position and an axis direction. It is the workhorse primitive for pipes, rods, wires, coils, bolt holes and cylindrical air domains; combined with Difference it also produces annuli and drilled holes. The layer properties split the cylinder radially or axially so that, for example, a pipe wall and its bore are created as one object with separate domains.
tools.usage: Component 1 > Geometry 1 > right-click > Cylinder   (Geometry toolbar > Cylinder)

parameters.name: r
parameters.description: Radius.

parameters.name: h
parameters.description: Height.

parameters.name: pos
parameters.description: double[] position of the base centre. Default {0,0,0}.

parameters.name: axis / axistype
parameters.description: Direction of the cylinder axis; axistype is x, y, z (default z), cartesian or spherical.

parameters.name: rot
parameters.description: Rotation about the axis.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: solid (default) or surface (a hollow tube wall).

parameters.name: layer, layerside, layertop, layerbottom
parameters.description: Layer thicknesses and the face they are measured from; layerside is the default and produces concentric shells.

parameters.name: selresult / contributeto
parameters.description: Create selections of the resulting objects / contribute to a cumulative selection.

tools.notes: With axistype spherical the axis property holds two angles instead of a 3-vector, and it is interpreted in the current angular unit (g.angularUnit("rad") or "deg"). Cone creates a truncated cone with rtop/ang, and ECone (Eccentric Cone) a cone whose top centre is offset. A cylinder used only as a cutting tool for Difference can be marked as construction geometry with setAttribute("construction", "on").

tools.name: Sphere
tools.description: Creates a solid ball or a surface sphere in 3D from a radius and a centre position. Use it for particles, droplets, inclusions, spherical air or infinite-element domains, and as a rounding tool in Boolean operations. The layer property produces concentric shells in one feature, which is the standard way to build a sphere with a surrounding absorbing or infinite-element layer without a second primitive and a Difference.
tools.usage: Component 1 > Geometry 1 > right-click > Sphere   (Geometry toolbar > Sphere)

parameters.name: r
parameters.description: Radius.

parameters.name: pos
parameters.description: double[] centre position. Default {0,0,0}.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: solid (default) or surface.

parameters.name: layer
parameters.description: double[] thicknesses of concentric layers, measured inwards from the outer radius.

parameters.name: axis / axistype / rot
parameters.description: Orientation of the local axis and rotation about it - relevant when layers or selections must be oriented.

parameters.name: sellayer / sellayershow
parameters.description: Create and expose selections for the individual layers.

parameters.name: selresult / contributeto
parameters.description: Create selections of the resulting objects / contribute to a cumulative selection.

tools.notes: Ellipsoid is the same feature with three semiaxes instead of one radius (property semiaxes). A surface sphere has no domain and cannot be meshed with tetrahedra - convert it with ConvertToSolid or use Cap Faces (Design Module / CAD Import Module) if you need a volume.

tools.name: Cone
tools.description: Creates a right circular cone or a cone frustum (truncated cone) in 3D. The top can be specified either by a top radius or by the half-angle of the cone, which makes it convenient for tapered pins, nozzles, chamfered shafts and conical horns. Like Cylinder it supports axial and side layers so a tapered wall can be produced as a separate domain of the same object.
tools.usage: Component 1 > Geometry 1 > right-click > Cone   (Geometry toolbar > Cone)

parameters.name: r
parameters.description: Bottom radius.

parameters.name: h
parameters.description: Height.

parameters.name: specifytop
parameters.description: Whether the top is given by a radius (rtop) or by the angle (ang).

parameters.name: rtop
parameters.description: Top radius of the frustum.

parameters.name: ang
parameters.description: Half-angle of the cone, in the geometry's angular unit.

parameters.name: pos
parameters.description: double[] position of the base centre.

parameters.name: axis / axistype / rot
parameters.description: Cone axis direction and rotation about it.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: solid (default) or surface.

parameters.name: layer, layerside, layertop, layerbottom
parameters.description: Layer thicknesses and the face they are applied from.

tools.notes: Set the angular unit on the sequence before writing an angle as a bare number - the API default for angles inside geometry features follows g.angularUnit(), while parameters can always carry an explicit [deg] or [rad]. ECone (Eccentric Cone) offsets the top circle relative to the bottom; Pyramid is the rectangular-base equivalent.

tools.name: Torus
tools.description: Creates a solid or surface torus in 3D from a major radius (centre of the tube to the axis) and a minor radius (tube radius), optionally only through a given angle so that a bend or elbow section is produced. Typical uses are O-rings, coils and windings, curved ducts and rounded transitions. Because the angle property makes partial tori, a Torus plus two Cylinders is often the fastest way to build a pipe bend without sweeping.
tools.usage: Component 1 > Geometry 1 > right-click > Torus   (Geometry toolbar > Torus)

parameters.name: rmaj
parameters.description: Major radius - distance from the torus axis to the centre of the tube.

parameters.name: rmin
parameters.description: Minor radius - radius of the tube.

parameters.name: angle
parameters.description: Revolution angle; less than a full turn gives a torus segment (elbow).

parameters.name: pos
parameters.description: double[] centre position.

parameters.name: axis / axistype / rot
parameters.description: Direction of the torus axis and rotation about it.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: solid (default) or surface.

parameters.name: intfaces
parameters.description: Keep the interior faces of the segment ends.

tools.notes: rmin must be smaller than rmaj or the torus self-intersects and the build fails. Helix (on the Geometry toolbar in 3D) is the related primitive for springs and helical coils. For a bend whose cross section is not circular, sweep a work-plane profile along a Bezier or parametric spine with Sweep instead.

tools.name: Rectangle
tools.description: Creates a solid (face) or curve rectangle in a 2D geometry or in a work plane's plane geometry. It is the basic 2D primitive for cross sections, computational boxes, plates and layered stacks, and is the usual profile fed to Extrude or Revolve to make a 3D object. The layer properties divide the rectangle into strips on any side, which builds a layered cross section as a single object with one domain per layer.
tools.usage: Component 1 > Geometry 1 > right-click > Rectangle (2D)   |   Component 1 > Geometry 1 > Work Plane 1 > Plane Geometry > right-click > Rectangle (3D)

parameters.name: size
parameters.description: double[] {lx, ly} - width and height. Default {1,1}.

parameters.name: pos
parameters.description: double[] position of the rectangle. Default {0,0}.

parameters.name: base
parameters.description: corner (default) or center - how pos is interpreted.

parameters.name: rot
parameters.description: Rotation angle about pos.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: solid (default, a face) or curve (edges only).

parameters.name: layer, layerleft, layerright, layertop, layerbottom
parameters.description: Layer thicknesses and the side they are measured from.

parameters.name: selresult / sellayer / contributeto
parameters.description: Create selections of the resulting objects or of the individual layers, and contribute to a cumulative selection.

tools.notes: Square is the same feature with a single side length. In 2D axisymmetric geometries the whole geometry must satisfy r >= 0 - Form Union removes anything at negative r. A curve rectangle has no face and cannot be extruded into a solid; use type solid for that.

tools.name: Circle
tools.description: Creates a disk (solid) or a circle (curve) in 2D or in a work plane, optionally only through a given angle to produce a sector. It is the profile of choice for round cross sections that will be extruded into cylinders or revolved into tori and spheres, and is the standard cutting tool for round holes in 2D. Concentric layers can be created directly with the layer property.
tools.usage: Component 1 > Geometry 1 > right-click > Circle (2D)   |   Work Plane 1 > Plane Geometry > right-click > Circle (3D)

parameters.name: r
parameters.description: Radius.

parameters.name: pos
parameters.description: double[] centre position.

parameters.name: angle
parameters.description: Sector angle; less than a full turn gives a circular sector or arc.

parameters.name: rot
parameters.description: Rotation of the sector about pos.

parameters.name: base
parameters.description: center (default) or corner.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: solid (default, a disk) or curve.

parameters.name: layer
parameters.description: double[] thicknesses of concentric layers measured inwards from r.

tools.notes: Ellipse is the same feature with a semiaxes pair instead of r. Circular Arc, Quadratic Bezier and Cubic Bezier (More Primitives) give single curve segments when you need to assemble an outline edge by edge rather than from closed primitives.

tools.name: Polygon
tools.description: Creates a curve or solid polygon from a list of vertex coordinates joined by straight line segments, in 2D, in a work plane, or as a 3D space curve. It is the fastest way to script an arbitrary outline: either type the coordinate columns directly, paste them as a table, or read them from a text file. A closed solid polygon becomes a face that Extrude, Revolve or Sweep can turn into a 3D object; an open curve polygon is typically used as a sweep spine or as a partition tool.
tools.usage: Component 1 > Geometry 1 > right-click > Polygon (2D)   |   Work Plane 1 > Plane Geometry > right-click > Polygon   |   3D: Geometry 1 > right-click > More Primitives > Polygon

parameters.name: source
parameters.description: Where the coordinates come from: a table typed in the Settings window, or a file.

parameters.name: x, y, z
parameters.description: Comma-separated coordinate lists, one property per axis (z only in 3D).

parameters.name: table
parameters.description: Coordinate table as an N-by-sdim array, an alternative to the x/y/z lists.

parameters.name: filename
parameters.description: Text file with the coordinates when source is file.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: solid (default, closed face) or open / curve - an open polyline.

parameters.name: workplane / workplanesrc
parameters.description: Work plane defining the coordinate system for a 3D polygon.

tools.notes: A solid polygon must be closed and non-self-intersecting; COMSOL closes the loop automatically from the last point back to the first. Use Bezier Polygon for outlines that mix straight and curved segments (property p holds the control points and degree the segment order), and Interpolation Curve to fit a smooth curve through a list of points from a table or file.

tools.name: Work Plane
tools.description: Defines a plane inside a 3D geometry and gives it its own nested 2D geometry sequence (Plane Geometry) where you draw the profile. The plane can be one of the coordinate planes with an offset (quickplane), a plane through three vertices, a plane parallel or normal to an existing face or edge, or a general plane through three coordinates. Work Plane is the hub of 3D modelling in COMSOL: nearly every non-primitive 3D shape is a profile drawn on a work plane and then extruded, revolved or swept, and a work plane also serves as a cutting tool for Partition Objects.
tools.usage: Component 1 > Geometry 1 > right-click > Work Plane, then draw under Geometry 1 > Work Plane 1 > Plane Geometry > right-click > Rectangle | Circle | Polygon ...

parameters.name: planetype
parameters.description: How the plane is defined: quick (a coordinate plane, the default), faceparallel, edgeangle, vertices, transformed, coordinates, normalvector, general, ... .

parameters.name: quickplane
parameters.description: Coordinate plane when planetype is quick: xy (default), yz or zx.

parameters.name: quickz / quickx / quicky
parameters.description: Offset of the quick plane along the normal axis.

parameters.name: face / edge / vertex1, vertex2, vertex3
parameters.description: Selections used by the faceparallel, edgeangle and vertices plane types.

parameters.name: genpoints
parameters.description: 3-by-sdim coordinate matrix defining a general plane, set element-wise with setIndex.

parameters.name: offset / offsettype / reverse
parameters.description: Offset the plane from its reference face and flip its normal.

parameters.name: unite
parameters.description: Unite the objects of the plane geometry before they are used by the following operation.

parameters.name: showworkplane / selplaneshow
parameters.description: Show the work plane and its selections in the 3D graphics.

tools.notes: The plane geometry is a full nested sequence reached with feature("wp1").geom() - primitives created there use 2D types (Rectangle, Circle, Polygon). Running only the work plane (g.run("wp1")) builds the profile without consuming it, which is what Extrude and Revolve expect. A work plane's own Finalize feature is optional and only needed when you want virtual operations inside the plane geometry. Related: Cross Section produces a 2D geometry from a 3D one, the inverse direction.

tools.name: Extrude
tools.description: Turns planar faces into 3D objects by sweeping them along the work-plane normal. The input is either the objects of a preceding work plane (the default) or planar faces already present in the 3D geometry, selected with the inputface selection. You can extrude several distances at once to create a stack of stacked domains in one feature, and optionally scale, twist or displace the extruded profile along the way, which covers tapered and twisted extrusions.
tools.usage: Component 1 > Geometry 1 > right-click > Extrude   (Geometry toolbar > Extrude)

parameters.name: distance
parameters.description: Extrusion distance, or a list of distances to produce several stacked sections.

parameters.name: extrudefrom
parameters.description: Whether the input is a work plane (default) or faces in the 3D geometry.

parameters.name: input
parameters.description: Selection of work-plane objects to extrude; defaults to all objects of the last preceding work plane.

parameters.name: inputface
parameters.description: Selection of planar faces to extrude when workplane is none.

parameters.name: workplane
parameters.description: Tag of the work plane that defines the extrusion direction.

parameters.name: reverse
parameters.description: Extrude in the opposite direction.

parameters.name: scale / displ / twist
parameters.description: Scale factors, in-plane displacement and twist angle applied at the end of each extrusion section.

parameters.name: includeinput / keep
parameters.description: Keep the input work-plane objects in the result.

parameters.name: selresult / contributeto
parameters.description: Create selections of the resulting objects / contribute to a cumulative selection.

tools.notes: Extrude consumes the work-plane objects unless includeinput/keep is on. Build the work plane first (g.run("wp1")) or the default input selection will be empty. Revolve is the rotational counterpart, Sweep follows an arbitrary spine curve, and Loft (Design Module) interpolates between several different profiles.

tools.name: Revolve
tools.description: Creates 3D objects by rotating planar faces about an axis, either the objects of a preceding work plane or planar faces in the 3D geometry. Give a start and end angle to make a full solid of revolution or only a wedge. Use it for anything axisymmetric that must nevertheless be modelled in 3D - shafts, vessels, lenses, nozzles - and for turning a 2D axisymmetric cross section into a 3D sector for a non-axisymmetric load.
tools.usage: Component 1 > Geometry 1 > right-click > Revolve   (Geometry toolbar > Revolve)

parameters.name: angle1 / angle2
parameters.description: Start and end angle of the revolution.

parameters.name: revolvefrom
parameters.description: Whether the input is a work plane (default) or faces in the 3D geometry.

parameters.name: input / intputface
parameters.description: Selections of the work-plane objects or the planar faces to revolve.

parameters.name: axis / axis3 / axistype
parameters.description: Revolution axis, in the work plane (2-vector) or in 3D (axis3).

parameters.name: pos / pos3
parameters.description: A point on the revolution axis.

parameters.name: workplane
parameters.description: Tag of the work plane that defines the plane of the profile.

parameters.name: origfaces / unite / keep
parameters.description: Keep the original faces, unite the result with the input objects, keep the input.

parameters.name: selresult / contributeto
parameters.description: Create selections of the resulting objects / contribute to a cumulative selection.

tools.notes: The profile must not cross the revolution axis or the build fails; touching the axis is allowed and produces a degenerate edge. Angles follow the sequence's angular unit (g.angularUnit("deg")). If the whole model is rotationally symmetric, a 2D axisymmetric component is far cheaper than revolving into 3D.

tools.name: Sweep
tools.description: Sweeps one or more faces, edges or points along a spine curve to create solids, surfaces or curves in 3D. Unlike Extrude and Revolve, the spine can be any curve - a polygon, a Bezier polygon, a parametric curve or an edge of an existing object - so Sweep is how you build pipes and ducts that follow a path, cable runs, channels and coils. Optional settings control how the cross section is oriented along the spine, whether it twists, and how it is matched to a different end profile.
tools.usage: Component 1 > Geometry 1 > right-click > Sweep   (Geometry toolbar > Sweep)

parameters.name: enttosweep
parameters.description: Selection of the faces, edges or points forming the cross section to sweep.

parameters.name: edge
parameters.description: Selection of the spine curve edges the cross section follows.

parameters.name: diredge / manualdir / reversedir
parameters.description: Control of the sweep direction along the spine.

parameters.name: enttomatch / vertextomatch / matchvertices
parameters.description: End cross section and the vertex correspondence used when the two profiles differ.

parameters.name: twist / twisting
parameters.description: Twist of the cross section along the spine.

parameters.name: scale
parameters.description: Scaling of the cross section along the spine.

parameters.name: spineperpend / spineperpstart / movetospine
parameters.description: Keep the cross section perpendicular to the spine and move it onto the spine start.

parameters.name: keep / includefinal / crossfaces
parameters.description: Keep the input objects, include the final profile, keep intermediate faces.

tools.notes: The spine must be smooth enough that the swept cross section does not self-intersect at tight corners - fillet the spine or split the sweep into sections if the build fails. Note the selection syntax for a work-plane object: "wp1.c1" refers to object c1 of work plane wp1. Loft (Design Module) is the alternative when the cross section changes shape along the path.

tools.name: Union
tools.description: Boolean operation that merges the selected geometry objects into one object. By default it keeps the interior boundaries between the original objects, so the result still has one domain per input - which is usually what you want, because each domain can then carry a different material. Clear Keep interior boundaries to fuse everything into a single domain. Union is used to assemble a model from primitives before finalization and to weld imported parts together.
tools.usage: Component 1 > Geometry 1 > right-click > Booleans and Partitions > Union   (Geometry toolbar > Booleans and Partitions > Union)

parameters.name: input
parameters.description: Selection of the objects to unite.

parameters.name: intbnd
parameters.description: on (default) keeps the interior boundaries between the input objects; off fuses them into one domain.

parameters.name: keep
parameters.description: Keep the input objects in addition to the result (default off).

parameters.name: repairtol / absrepairtol / repairtoltype
parameters.description: Relative or absolute tolerance used when merging nearly coincident entities.

parameters.name: propagatesel
parameters.description: on (default) propagates selections from the input objects to the result.

parameters.name: selresult / selresultshow / contributeto
parameters.description: Create selections of the resulting objects, choose which levels are exposed, contribute to a cumulative selection.

tools.notes: Intersection (type "Intersection", with keeplowerdim for lower-dimensional intersections) and Compose (type "Compose", driven by a set formula in the formula property where + is union, * is intersection and - is difference) are created exactly the same way. Union is not the same as Form Union: this feature merges selected objects mid-sequence, while Form Union is the final step that combines everything that is left.

tools.name: Difference
tools.description: Boolean operation that subtracts one set of objects from another: the objects in input2 are removed from the union of the objects in input. This is how holes, slots, pockets, cavities and fluid domains inside a solid are made - build the negative volume as a primitive and subtract it. Both the objects to add and the objects to subtract can optionally be kept, which is useful when the same cutting tool is reused several times.
tools.usage: Component 1 > Geometry 1 > right-click > Booleans and Partitions > Difference   (Geometry toolbar > Booleans and Partitions > Difference)

parameters.name: input
parameters.description: Selection of the objects to add (the body being cut).

parameters.name: input2
parameters.description: Selection of the objects to subtract (the cutting tools).

parameters.name: keepadd
parameters.description: Keep the input objects to add (default off).

parameters.name: keepsubtract
parameters.description: Keep the input objects to subtract (default off) - use it when the same tool is subtracted more than once.

parameters.name: intbnd
parameters.description: Keep interior boundaries in the result (default on).

parameters.name: repairtol / absrepairtol / repairtoltype
parameters.description: Tolerance used to decide whether nearly coincident faces are treated as coincident.

parameters.name: propagatesel
parameters.description: Propagate the input objects' selections to the result (default on).

tools.notes: A cutting tool that only touches a face without passing through it produces zero-thickness slivers and repair warnings - make the tool overshoot the body. If a Difference produces unexpected extra faces, raise repairtol or set repairtoltype to absolute. Delete Entities (API type "Delete") is the alternative when you want to remove a face or domain from an already-built object rather than subtract a solid.

tools.name: Partition Objects
tools.description: Splits 2D and 3D geometry objects into several domains using other objects as tool objects, or, in 3D, using a work plane as an infinite cutting plane. Unlike Difference, nothing is removed: the object keeps its outer shape but gains internal boundaries. Use it to create a boundary layer region, to separate a region for a finer mesh or for a different material, to cut a symmetric model in half, or to give the sweep mesher the block structure it needs.
tools.usage: Component 1 > Geometry 1 > right-click > Booleans and Partitions > Partition Objects   (Geometry toolbar > Booleans and Partitions > Partition Objects)

parameters.name: input
parameters.description: Selection of the objects to partition.

parameters.name: partitionwith
parameters.description: objects (default) - use the tool objects in tool; workplane - use the plane of the work plane named in workplane.

parameters.name: tool
parameters.description: Selection of the tool objects when partitionwith is objects.

parameters.name: workplane
parameters.description: Tag of the work plane used as the cutting plane.

parameters.name: keepinput / keeptool
parameters.description: Keep the input and tool objects in addition to the result.

parameters.name: repairtol / absrepairtol / repairtoltype
parameters.description: Tolerance used when the cut is nearly tangent to an existing face.

parameters.name: propagatesel / selresult / contributeto
parameters.description: Selection propagation and creation of selections from the result.

tools.notes: The GUI node is called Partition Objects but the API feature type is "Partition". The related features are PartitionDomains (cut domains with curves, surfaces or extended faces), PartitionFaces and PartitionEdges, all reachable from the same Booleans and Partitions menu. Split (type "Split") is the opposite idea: it explodes one object into separate objects, one per domain, face, edge or vertex.

tools.name: Array
tools.description: Replicates the selected objects into a linear, rectangular or block-shaped pattern given by a displacement vector and a count per direction. It is the efficient way to build repeated features - hole patterns, fin stacks, electrode arrays, unit cells - because the whole pattern remains one feature whose counts can be parameters and can be changed in one place. Combine with Difference to drill a whole grid of holes in one operation.
tools.usage: Component 1 > Geometry 1 > right-click > Transforms > Array   (Geometry toolbar > Transforms > Array)

parameters.name: input
parameters.description: Selection of the objects to replicate.

parameters.name: size
parameters.description: Number of copies in each direction, e.g. "2 2 1".

parameters.name: displ
parameters.description: Displacement between neighbouring copies in each direction, e.g. "4 4 0".

parameters.name: propagatesel
parameters.description: Propagate the input objects' selections to the copies (default on).

parameters.name: selresult / selresultshow / contributeto
parameters.description: Create selections of the resulting objects and contribute to a cumulative selection.

parameters.name: color / customcolor
parameters.description: Colour of the resulting selection in the Graphics window.

tools.notes: Array consumes its input objects; the count includes the original, so size "2 2 1" gives four objects in total. For a circular pattern use Rotate with a list of angles and keep set to on, or Copy plus Rotate, since Array is translational only.

tools.name: Move
tools.description: Translates the selected objects by a displacement vector, or places them so that a chosen source point lands on a chosen destination point. Use it to position primitives that were created at the origin, to align an imported part with the rest of the model, or - with keep on - to produce a translated duplicate. The Copy feature is the same operation with the input objects retained by default.
tools.usage: Component 1 > Geometry 1 > right-click > Transforms > Move   (Geometry toolbar > Transforms > Move)

parameters.name: input
parameters.description: Selection of the objects to move.

parameters.name: displx, disply, displz
parameters.description: Displacement components (also settable together through the displ matrix).

parameters.name: specify
parameters.description: Whether the move is given as a displacement or by matching an old position to a new position.

parameters.name: oldpos / oldposvertex / oldposcoord
parameters.description: Source point, given as coordinates or as a picked vertex.

parameters.name: newpos / newposvertices / newposx, newposy, newposz
parameters.description: Destination point, given as coordinates or as a picked vertex.

parameters.name: propagatesel / selresult / contributeto
parameters.description: Selection propagation and creation of selections from the result.

parameters.name: workplane / workplanesrc
parameters.description: Work plane whose coordinate system the displacement is expressed in.

tools.notes: Move and Copy are the same documented feature pair - Move consumes the input, Copy keeps it. Scale (type "Scale", properties factor and pos) resizes about a point and can use different factors per axis. Rigid Transform combines a rotation and a translation in one feature.

tools.name: Rotate
tools.description: Rotates the selected objects about a point in 2D or about an axis in 3D, by one angle or by a list of angles. Use it to orient a primitive that was built along a coordinate axis, to align an imported part, and - by giving several angles with keep on - to build a circular pattern of copies, which is the rotational counterpart of Array. In 3D the axis can be given as a vector, as Euler angles, or by picking an existing edge.
tools.usage: Component 1 > Geometry 1 > right-click > Transforms > Rotate   (Geometry toolbar > Transforms > Rotate)

parameters.name: input
parameters.description: Selection of the objects to rotate.

parameters.name: rot
parameters.description: Rotation angle, or a comma-separated list of angles to produce several rotated copies.

parameters.name: pos
parameters.description: Point the rotation is about (2D) or a point on the rotation axis (3D).

parameters.name: axis / axistype / ax2 / ax3
parameters.description: Rotation axis in 3D; axistype is x, y, z, cartesian or spherical.

parameters.name: eulerang
parameters.description: Euler angles, as an alternative to a single axis and angle.

parameters.name: edge / specify
parameters.description: Use a picked edge as the rotation axis; specify chooses how the axis is defined.

parameters.name: keep
parameters.description: Keep the input objects, so the feature produces rotated copies.

tools.notes: Angles use the sequence's angular unit (g.angularUnit("deg") or "rad"); parameters may carry an explicit [deg]. Rotating around an axis that does not pass through the object's own centre requires a pos on that axis - a common source of surprises. Related transforms: Move, Copy, Mirror, Scale and Rigid Transform.

tools.name: Mirror
tools.description: Reflects the selected objects in a plane (3D), a line (2D) or a point (1D), defined by a point on the plane and its normal. With Keep input objects on it is the standard way to build a symmetric model from one half - mirror, then Union the two halves - and with keep off it simply flips an object that was built the wrong way round. The mirror plane can also be given by picking an existing edge.
tools.usage: Component 1 > Geometry 1 > right-click > Transforms > Mirror   (Geometry toolbar > Transforms > Mirror)

parameters.name: input
parameters.description: Selection of the objects to reflect.

parameters.name: pos
parameters.description: A point on the mirror plane / line.

parameters.name: axis
parameters.description: Normal of the mirror plane (3D) or of the mirror line (2D).

parameters.name: keep
parameters.description: Keep the input objects, producing a mirrored copy alongside the original.

parameters.name: edge / specify
parameters.description: Define the mirror line by a picked edge instead of a normal vector.

parameters.name: propagatesel / selresult / contributeto
parameters.description: Selection propagation and creation of selections from the result.

tools.notes: Mirroring and then uniting leaves a coincident interior boundary on the symmetry plane - set intbnd to off on the Union if you want a single domain. If the model really is symmetric, meshing and solving only half with a symmetry boundary condition is usually cheaper than mirroring the geometry.

tools.name: Fillet
tools.description: Rounds selected corners of 2D geometry objects with a circular arc of a given radius. Filleting removes the stress and field singularities that sharp re-entrant corners produce, and also improves mesh quality, so it is routinely applied to 2D cross sections before extruding them. Vertices that cannot be filleted with the requested radius are skipped, but a fillet that runs into a neighbouring edge raises an error.
tools.usage: Component 1 > Geometry 1 > right-click > Fillet (2D)   (Geometry toolbar > Fillet)

parameters.name: point
parameters.description: Selection of the vertices to round, given as object(index) plus vertex numbers.

parameters.name: radius
parameters.description: Fillet radius.

parameters.name: pointinsketch / selectinsketch
parameters.description: Pick the vertices in the sketch view instead of the object.

parameters.name: selresult / selresultshow / contributeto
parameters.description: Create selections of the resulting objects and contribute to a cumulative selection.

tools.notes: In the base package Fillet and Chamfer (type "Chamfer", property dist) work on 2D objects only. 3D fillets and chamfers require the Design Module, where the API types are Fillet3D and Chamfer3D and the selection is made on edges rather than vertices. The Design Module also adds Loft, Midsurface, Thicken, Cap Faces and Knit to Solid; the CAD Import Module adds Import of 3D CAD files plus the Defeaturing and Repair tools (Delete Fillets, Delete Holes, Delete Short Edges, Delete Sliver Faces, Delete Small Faces, Delete Spikes, Detach Faces, Repair). Remove Details (type "RemoveDetails") is in the base package and cleans up small entities automatically.

tools.name: Form Union
tools.description: The finalization step that always sits last in a geometry sequence. Form Union combines every remaining object into one geometry object whose domains correspond to the input objects and their overlaps, so that touching parts share conforming boundaries and the mesh is continuous across them. Switching the node to Form Assembly instead keeps the objects separate and creates identity or contact pairs between touching boundaries - the right choice for mechanical contact, for parts that slide, and for non-conforming meshes.
tools.usage: Component 1 > Geometry 1 > Form Union (the last node; select it and change Action to Form an assembly to turn it into Form Assembly)

parameters.name: action
parameters.description: union (default) - merge everything into one object; assembly - keep the objects separate.

parameters.name: createpairs
parameters.description: on (default) - create pairs between touching boundaries when action is assembly.

parameters.name: pairtype
parameters.description: identity (default) or contact - the kind of pair created.

parameters.name: imprint
parameters.description: off by default - imprint the touching boundaries onto each other when action is assembly.

parameters.name: splitpairs
parameters.description: off by default - create one pair per connected set of touching boundaries instead of a single pair.

parameters.name: frame
parameters.description: Frame used for the automatically generated Identity pairs: spatial (default), mesh, geometry or material.

parameters.name: repairtol / absrepairtol / repairtoltype
parameters.description: Tolerance deciding when nearly coincident entities are merged.

tools.notes: The only allowed tag for this feature is "fin", and there can be exactly one per sequence; it is added automatically to every component geometry (but not to geometry parts or work-plane sequences, where you create it manually only if you need virtual operations). g.run() builds everything including Form Union and the virtual operations, while g.run(<ftag>) stops at a named feature and g.runPre(<ftag>) stops just before it. In 1D and 2D axisymmetric geometries the union action also discards anything at r < 0.

tools.name: Import (geometry)
tools.description: Reads an external geometry into the sequence. One Import feature handles every supported source: COMSOL's own MPHBIN/MPHTXT objects, 3D CAD files, mesh and 3D-printing files (STL, PLY, 3MF, VRML), 2D DXF drawings, ECAD layouts, and geometry sequences stored in another MPH-file. COMSOL sets the type property from the file extension, and the rest of the settings - repair tolerance, which object kinds to keep, whether to knit surfaces into solids - then control how the imported entities are cleaned up before they join the sequence.
tools.usage: Component 1 > Geometry 1 > right-click > Import   (Geometry toolbar > Import)

parameters.name: filename
parameters.description: Path of the file to import.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Set automatically from the file: native for MPHBIN/MPHTXT, cad for 3D CAD files, and other values for mesh, DXF, ECAD and geometry-sequence imports.

parameters.name: importtol
parameters.description: Absolute repair tolerance applied to the imported CAD entities (default 1e-5).

parameters.name: repair / simplify / removeredundant
parameters.description: Repair the imported objects, simplify their underlying curves and surfaces, and remove redundant edges and vertices.

parameters.name: knit / fillholes
parameters.description: Knit surface objects into solids (solid, surface or off) and try to generate faces for missing geometry.

parameters.name: keepsolid / keepbnd / keepfree
parameters.description: Which object kinds to import: solids (on), surfaces (on), free curves and points (off).

parameters.name: unit
parameters.description: source (default) - take the length unit from the file; current - interpret the numbers in the geometry's own unit.

parameters.name: selresult / selindividual
parameters.description: Create selections for all imported objects, and for each individual imported object, so that physics and materials can address them by name.

tools.notes: Importing ACIS, IGES, Parasolid, STEP, CATIA V5, Inventor, NX, Creo, Pro/ENGINEER, SOLIDWORKS or AutoCAD files requires the CAD Import Module, the Design Module or a LiveLink for CAD product; CATIA V5 needs the File Import for CATIA V5 add-on. Only MPHBIN/MPHTXT, mesh (STL/PLY/3MF/VRML) and DXF import work with the base package. importData() embeds the file in the MPH-file instead of referencing it on disk. Imported CAD models often need Remove Details or the Defeaturing and Repair tools before they mesh well.
